title: Truncation not reported as truncation
description: The provider stopped at the output token limit, but the library reports a normal finish, a generic parse error, or a partial result as success.
effect: Agents accept partial output or retry without raising the limit, and structured pipelines ingest incomplete records.

title: Finish reason mapped to the wrong value
description: The library maps the provider's finish value to a different canonical value, drops it, or fails on a value it doesn't know.
effect: Code that branches on the finish reason takes the wrong branch, for example treating a content filter or a new value as a normal stop.

title: Token usage misreported
description: The library reports token counts that differ from the provider's: cached or reasoning tokens are dropped or double-counted, or streamed usage is lost.
effect: Cost and quota tracking is off, most often on cached prompts and reasoning models.

title: Streamed content or completion state corrupted
description: The library corrupts streamed text, for example at multi-byte character boundaries, or reports a stream that ended early as complete.
effect: Corrupted or unfinished text is treated as the final answer.

title: Tool calls lost, merged or returned with broken arguments
description: The library drops or merges tool calls, mixes up their ids, or returns a call as complete while its arguments are cut off or repaired.
effect: Tools run with wrong or incomplete arguments, or don't run at all.

title: Provider errors surfaced as the wrong kind of error, or not at all
description: The library reports a provider error as a different kind of error, loses details such as the retry delay, or returns an error as a normal result.
effect: Retries and backoff misbehave, and callers can't tell a rate limit from a bad request.

title: The library sends something the caller didn't ask for
description: The library adds, drops or renames request fields the caller didn't set, or sends a combination the provider rejects.
effect: Calls fail on current models, or behave differently from what the caller configured.
